item.title: MOLAR DISTALIZATION. A CASE‑BASED CONSIDERATIONS AND PERSPECTIVES
item.description: Molar distalization is a method used to resolve class II malocclusions in order to correct distalized molar relationships, but it also represents an effective tool of arch lengthening and regaining space in cases of mesioposition of the first molars following caries or premature loss of decidous teeth. item.title: A REVIEW OF THE LINK BETWEEN ARTIFICIAL FOOD COLORINGS AND ATTENTION DEFICIT HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER AND DENTAL HEALTH
item.description: Artificial food colorings (AFCs) are widely used in processed foods, beverages, and snacks. Recent studies suggest that these additives may influence behavior and cognitive functions, particularly in children and adults with attention‑deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). item.title: A BIOANTHROPOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVE ON DENTAL HEALTH AND MORPHOLOGICAL VARIATION IN IRON AGE HUMAN POPULATIONS FROM DOBROGEA (ROMANIA)
item.description: This study investigates the oral health status and dental morphological traits of an Iron Age population from the Dobrogea region (southeastern Romania), based on the macroscopic analysis of 226 teeth from 32 adult individuals recovered from the necropolises of Histria, Isaccea, and Enisala. item.title: BRAIN MECHANISMS OF CRUNCHY FOOD PROCESSING, THEIR IMPLICATIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND THE EFFECTS OF CRUNCHY FOODS ON DENTHAL HEALTH
item.description: Crunchy foods, characterized by their distinctive texture and sound, elicit strong multisensory responses that engage both somatosensory and auditory pathways in the brain. item.title: STUDYING HUMAN DENTITION IN ARCHAEOLOGICAL POPULATIONS: MAIN DIRECTIONS OF RESEARCH
item.description: This paper provides a survey of current research directions on the teeth belonging to archaeological human populations. The study of dental structures offers insights into estimating age at death, health status, paleodiet, and the use of teeth as a “third hand” and for cultural purposes. item.title: STRATEGIES FOR THE SCIENTIFIC VALORIZATION OF RESEARCH ON OXIDATIVE STRESS BIOMARKERS IN MINIMAL TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURIES ASSOCIATED WITH OCCUPATIONAL WHOLE-BODY VIBRATION EXPOSURE AND DENTAL ASPECTS
item.description: Minimal traumatic brain injury (mi-TBI) associated with occupational whole-body vibration (WBV) is an under-recognized condition that can lead to cumulative oxidative stress and progressive neurodegeneration. item.title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIABETES AND DENTAL HEALTH IN COMPANION ANIMALS. PREVALENCE STUDIES
item.description: Diabetes mellitus in companion animals is associated with a high prevalence of dental disorders, including gingivitis, periodontal disease, dental calculus, and abscess formation. item.title: EFFECTS OF SPIRULINA ON ORAL HEALTH. A REVIEW OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE ON GINGIVITIS AND PERIODONTITIS
item.description: Spirulina, a blue-green algae with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, has been investigated as an adjunct therapy in oral health. This review summarizes clinical evidence on the effects of spirulina on gingivitis and periodontitis, focusing on plaque reduction, decreased gingival inflammation, and enhanced tissue healing. item.title: AN EDITORIAL VIEW ON THE OCCUPATIONAL WHOLE-BODY VIBRATION AND PSYCHOPHYSICAL STRESS. EMERGING LINKS BETWEEN OXIDATIVE IMBALANCE AND TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT ARTHRITIS
item.description: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthritis is a degenerative and inflammatory condition influenced by mechanical loading, oxidative stress, and neuroendocrine factors. Occupational exposure to whole-body vibration (WBV), especially when combined with psychophysical stress, may intensify oxidative imbalance and inflammatory injury in TMJ tissues. item.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) appears as a transforming force in dentistry, promising optimization of diagnosis, medical triage and work flow automatization.
